schedule.emptyHint: Create a schedule and the VPN will connect and disconnect on its own.
schedule.serverHint: The schedule connects to this server. “Current server” takes the server selected when you save the schedule.
schedule.localHint: Traffic goes through the local proxy (Happ, for example), so no server is picked here.
schedule.captureHint: Tunnel takes all traffic; Proxy takes the programs that use the system proxy.
schedule.tunUnavailable: The tunnel needs the helper service: without it the schedule cannot connect.
schedule.unavailable: Unavailable: the tunnel needs the helper service

problem.name: Enter a name
problem.server: The chosen server was deleted: pick another one or “Current server”

splitTunneling.invalidProcess: Invalid process name. Example: curl.exe or yt-dlp

scope.label: Only selected apps
scope.hintAll: Every app uses the VPN. Turn this on to keep it for apps with the route “VPN”.
scope.hintAllProxy: Programs that use the system proxy go through the VPN; the rest connect directly. Turn this on to keep it for apps with the route “VPN”.
scope.hintListed: Only apps with the route “VPN” use the VPN; the rest connect directly. Your site rules apply to every app.
scope.hintListedProxy: Only apps with the route “VPN” use the VPN, if they use the system proxy; the rest connect directly. Your site rules apply to every app.
scope.hintEmpty: No app has the route “VPN” yet. Only sites in your “VPN” rules and, with Smart RU, sites blocked in Russia use the VPN.
scope.pending: The current connection keeps the previous setting; the new one applies from the next connection.
scope.olderService: The helper service is an older version: in Tunnel mode every app still uses the VPN.

routing.title: Happ routing
routing.hint: Add a Happ routing profile to your own rules: paste a happ://routing/… link or pick a subscription's profile. You see what changes first.
routing.off: The provider turns its routing off. Your rules stay as they are.
routing.addTitle: Will be added to your rules: {{count}}
routing.smartRuTurnOn: Smart RU will be turned on: Russian sites go direct.
routing.smartRuAlreadyOn: Smart RU is already on: Russian sites go direct.
routing.nothingToAdd: Nothing to add: everything is in place or not carried over.
routing.noteLocal: the local network always goes direct
routing.noteNotShipped: this list is not in the app
routing.keptRest: The provider sends the rest direct; here it goes through the VPN
routing.keptDns: The profile's DNS ({{servers}}): your DNS settings stay
routing.overLimit: {{count}} did not fit: the list holds up to 10,000 rules.
routing.whereRules: You can edit or remove them in Settings, under Domain routing.
routing.nextConnect: Changes apply from the next connection.
routing.stale: The profile changed: review it again.
